findings.summary: L3 validity keys are measured and recorded but are not integrated into replay invalidation. ReceiptReplayer validates receipt fields and ancestry only; it does not load or compare the previously sealed validity key for product tree, SPEC, target identity, or PR identity. Consequently changes to those facts can still reuse previously accepted implementation/review receipts instead of invalidating the affected stages and triggering re-verification/review.

Typed target-competition feedback is not connected to a lifecycle recovery transition. MergeStage classifies target competition, but _publish_release raises StageRefused and MergeStage.act re-raises it; the pipeline terminalizes the run as refused. No reconfigure/retry path is selected, so target competition is operationally handled as a terminal refusal rather than the distinct non-content outcome required by L6.

L7 raw-event records do not reliably carry opaque Runtime run/session/receipt references. The observed history entries include stage, attempt, output_commit and optional validity, but omit sealed receipt and runtime reference data; last_receipt and receipt_digests remain internal pipeline state and are not emitted by _record or persist_event. The raw-event boundary therefore cannot preserve the complete traceability required for recovery and query.
